title: Open-Vocabulary Models and Label Propagation for Uncertainty-aware Pseudo-Labeling of Object Detection Datasets

problem.summary: Object detection models rely on large-scale annotated datasets that require substantial manual annotation effort.
statements: Object detection models rely on large-scale annotated datasets that require substantial manual annotation effort.
The labeling costs further increase when annotation uncertainty is captured through soft labels, as multiple annotations must be collected for each object.
We address this challenge by introducing a semi-supervised framework for the uncertaintyaware annotation of object detection datasets.

background.summary: Our approach leverages open-vocabulary object detectors to generate region proposals and semantically meaningful object representations.

evidence.quote: Our approach leverages open-vocabulary object detectors to generate region proposals and semantically meaningful object representations.
Based on these representations, we construct an object-level similarity graph and propagate probabilistic label information.

solution.summary: Furthermore, we show that detectors trained on semiautomatically annotated data achieve performance comparable to models trained on fully manually annotated data.
solution.approach: Furthermore, we show that detectors trained on semiautomatically annotated data achieve performance comparable to models trained on fully manually annotated data.
components: We achieve state-of-the-art downstream detection performance for the task of semi-supervised object detection on the COCO dataset, with 40.5% AP virtually matching the performance of the model trained on fully manually constructed data (40.9%) at only 1% of labeling costs.
These results highlight the potential of open-vocabulary models and graph-based label propagation for efficient, accurate and uncertainty-aware pseudo-labeling.
I NTRODUCTION Modern object detectors rely on large-scale annotated datasets, whose creation requires substantial manual effort.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, we show that detectors trained on semiautomatically annotated data achieve performance comparable to models trained on fully manually annotated data.

We achieve state-of-the-art downstream detection performance for the task of semi-supervised object detection on the COCO dataset, with 40.5% AP virtually matching the performance of the model trained on fully manually constructed data (40.9%) at only 1% of labeling costs.
